claim_001.label: SUPPORTED
claim_001.text: Black reads .gitignore files using the utf-8-sig encoding so that a UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the file is skipped before the ignore patterns are parsed.

evidence.note: The frozen diff changes the encoding used by get_gitignore from utf-8 to utf-8-sig and adds a comment explaining that the UTF-8 byte order mark is skipped.
The added regression test writes root and nested .gitignore files with utf-8-sig and verifies that only the non-ignored Python files are collected.

claim_001.rationale: The source change directly selects an encoding that consumes the UTF-8 byte order mark, and the regression test verifies the resulting source-collection behavior for both root and nested .gitignore files.

claim_002.label: SUPPORTED
claim_002.text: The encoding change was made because an unskipped UTF-8 byte order mark became part of the first .gitignore pattern, causing that pattern not to match.

evidence.note: The added source comment states that without skipping the byte order mark it becomes part of the first pattern, which then never matches.
The commit title states: Skip UTF-8 BOM when reading .gitignore.
The changelog explains that the mark became part of the first pattern, so that pattern never matched and Black formatted files ignored by Git.

claim_002.rationale: The frozen source comment, commit title, and changelog explicitly identify the unskipped byte order mark and the resulting failure of the first ignore pattern as the reason for the change.

claim_003.label: UNSUPPORTED
claim_003.text: The change was primarily introduced to improve the performance of Black's .gitignore processing.
claim_003.rationale: The frozen evidence describes correctness for UTF-8 byte order marks and does not identify performance as an objective.

claim_004.label: UNSUPPORTED
claim_004.text: The change adds support for a new .gitignore pattern syntax that was previously rejected by Black.
claim_004.rationale: The pattern parser and supported pattern syntax are unchanged. The frozen change only alters how the .gitignore file is decoded before its existing patterns are parsed.
